# 096-symbol-sweep — info

*Generated by `104` from the folds in `096-symbol-sweep.lua`. Do not edit this page;
edit the program and run the sweep again.*

**An instrument** — phase 14. Not part of the machine, and it does not ship
to whoever builds one.

## What it is

Writes one companion page per blueprint, from the blueprint's own
declarations and the ledger's reverse index. Nobody edits these; they are
rebuilt, and the header of each one says so.

For a general reader: the project's rule is that a thing is written once. A
page describing a blueprint's interface, written by hand, would be the same
information twice, and the second copy is always the one that goes stale. So
this generates them. What a companion page adds that the blueprint does not
already say is the direction nobody can see from inside one file: what
consumes this. Change a number here and that list is what breaks.

## What it offers

| call | takes | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `M.run` | `dir, opts` | Rewrite the companion page beside every blueprint, and report which blueprints are thin. |
| `M.report` | `R, out` | The coverage report: how many pages were written, and the four ways a blueprint can be thin -- declaring nothing, asserting nothing, drawing nothin... |

### In the author's words

**`M.run`**

Rewrite the companion page beside every blueprint, and report which
blueprints are thin.

Pass `dry` in the options to work out everything and write nothing, which is
how to see what a change would do to two hundred pages before doing it.

**`M.report`**

The coverage report: how many pages were written, and the four ways a
blueprint can be thin -- declaring nothing, asserting nothing, drawing
nothing, or publishing only symbols nothing reads.

## How it works inside

Nothing outside this file can call these. They are listed so a reader
knows what is in it, not how — a companion page treats a function as a
box with a label on it.

| function | takes | what it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `shown` | `L, name` | A resolved value in the unit its author declared it in. |
| `sorted_copy` | `t` | *(no description in the source)* |
| `consumes` | `L, bp` | Every symbol this blueprint's derivations and constraints reach for, that it did not declare itself, with the blueprint that owns each. |
| `page` | `L, bp` | *(no description in the source)* |

## What it reads

`091`, `092`, `094`. Every instrument here reaches for its dependencies with `dofile`
against a hard-coded project root rather than with `require`, because
there is no package path to configure and a root that can be overridden
by an argument is this project's convention for anything runnable.

## Running it

Both. Something else can load it, and a person can run it:

    luajit src/096-symbol-sweep.lua [project-directory]

---

*Every function in this project is wrapped in a vimfold that opens with a
comment carrying its name, followed by prose, followed by the definition.
That was adopted so a long file collapses neatly in an editor. It is also,
by accident, a machine-readable statement of what a module offers, and it
is the only reason this page can exist — Lua itself says nothing about what
a file exports.*
